candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13/PDF p.17: Monitor results of diagnostic and laboratory tests
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — A1C interpretation
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the current ADA A1C diagnostic threshold and confirmation requirement when interpreting repeated abnormal A1C results.

options.A: The repeated results meet and confirm the ADA A1C criterion for diabetes.
options.B: The results are in the ADA prediabetes range because diabetes requires an A1C above 7.0%.
options.C: A1C cannot be used to diagnose diabetes and is only used after treatment begins.
options.D: The results establish hypoglycemia because both values are below 7.0%.

candidate.rationale: ADA 2026 lists A1C at least 6.5% as a diagnostic criterion for diabetes. In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, diagnosis requires confirmatory testing; two abnormal results from the same test at different time points can provide that confirmation. Both 6.7% and 6.6% are above the 6.5% threshold, so A is correct. Prediabetes is A1C 5.7-6.4%, and A1C is an accepted diagnostic test when appropriately performed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A1C >=6.5% is a diabetes diagnostic criterion; absent unequivocal hyperglycemia, two abnormal test results are required for confirmation, including repeat abnormal A1C results at different time points.
candidate.source_document_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Table 2.1: A1C >=6.5% criterion; Confirming the Diagnosis section: in absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, two abnormal results are required and may be the same test at two different time points; Table 2.2: A1C 5.7-6.4% defines prediabetes
candidate.source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1)
candidate.stem: A nonpregnant adult without unequivocal hyperglycemia has an A1C of 6.7%. A repeat A1C obtained promptly is 6.6%. How should the nurse interpret these results using ADA 2026 criteria?
